catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class re-enables a heater output after a safety reset. This input-free reenable action restores the configured control mode (default Closed Loop) with OUTMODE and reads the mode back; the safe-state action is the stop.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's helper field is PythonObjectDriver (family python-object) but its decision is direct-driver; this package is a direct Driver over instruments.ls336:DeviceConnection, as the decision and the exemplar select. The card lists three unrelated DeviceConnection entry symbols (dp832, ls336, zaber_motor) and its read/write hints mix the ls336 class with the cs4/cm4g magnet classes; this package integrates the ls336 Lake Shore 336, the entry that matches the thermal.setpoint candidate class and the per-channel heater/PID/mode/range hints. The hardware factory is .native:connect. It imports devices.instruments.ls336.DeviceConnection, so a deployment must mount the clone as the package devices (README.md:5, README.md:102-119) and provide pythonSoftIOC, which the clone's base modules import (base_device.py:3); the card's install block installs nothing. A live run also needs a TCP/serial-adapter endpoint and the deployment options channel (1 or 2), setpoint_unit (K, Cel or [degF], default K) and reenable_mode (default Closed Loop). The factory has never been run; no hardware is attached and no network was used. The clone has no simulator, mock or test fixture for DeviceConnection, so fake.py is an in-memory F0 stand-in, not a recording: every starting value is marked placeholder in the source and there is no plant model or timing. The clone does not state the SETP unit, so setpoint fields are published in Celsius and converted with the setpoint_unit option. Not covered: the second heater output (this resource controls one configured output), PID writes (the clone states no gain units or ranges, so PID is read only), ramp/wait/tolerance behaviour, the soft-IOC Device/PV layer, and the controller's sensor curves. MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked against the clone at the pin, native.py line by line: serving the LS336 DeviceConnection is a sound pick among the card's three entry symbols (the one its read/write hints and thermal class describe), R2 fits a heater controller, every limit is sourced (heater_range menu, ls336.py:18) or operator_required, and the stop is source-backed and confirmed: the e-stop and the safe-state action send OUTMODE <channel>,0,<channel>,0, the upstream's own Off entry sent as do_sets sends it (ls336.py:17, 62-63), the action confirms mode 0 with a fresh OUTMODE? read, and the declared re-enable (no @reset hook) restores a control mode; a controller that ignores Off or never answers ends the e-stop MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held, and a probe of an e-stop during an in-flight command answered command_in_flight, then the background retry confirmed it. Defects fixed: the stop discarded the mode set_outmode reads back, so a receipt said native engaged against the reply (it now fails unless Off), and its docstring and facts.md said it waits for no readback although set_outmode waits up to 2 s; safe_state omitted that the stop also sets the output's control input to input <channel> and powerup enable to 0 and leaves the other output heating; the pid read claimed the configured loop although read_pid sends PID? without the output number (ls336.py:143), and the fake followed the channel; setpoint_unit defaulted to K on hardware, so a Celsius-configured controller would get SETP 303.15 for an envelope-checked 30 Cel (the hardware backend now refuses setpoint reads, writes and the thermal action until the unit is declared, superseding the author's note 'default K'); three facts reached past their cited lines (PVs 'per configured channel', menu indices and control input at ls336.py:62-65, reads and writes through self.tn at telnet_base.py:27-36) and two were added (the README's other devices, read_until's partial return on timeout). The reviewer changed driver.py, fake.py (float readbacks as the upstream parses them, control input and powerup kept, a channel-independent PID reply, set_pid dropped), test_driver.py (the e-stop receipt and the reset's no-re-enable asserted; new cases for channel 2's control input with output 1 left on, an ignored Off, a silent controller and the hardware unit rule; ten package cases and the stock gate case pass) and facts.md (rewritten: scope, the unit, the stop path, upstream transport behaviour, licence), and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; native.py, driver.lock.json, RESULT.json, site-limits.example.json and task.json are unchanged. The gate and collect.py --strict pass with no finding and the digest unchanged (sha256:c8ad76766c8e629f685a2ec86410ed3a070ee6aecb6507d09708b40693a380ff). The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: R2 heater controller; the loader refuses the hardware backend until a human signs. Before a hardware run: confirm in the Model 336 manual that OUTMODE mode 0 turns the output off (the clone only names the menu entry Off); the stop and the re-enable write control input <channel> (the upstream's output n, input n convention), so on a controller wired otherwise the first e-stop changes the control input and any later closed-loop start, front panel included, regulates on that input; set setpoint_unit to the control input's unit (KRDG is Kelvin, SETP uses the input's unit); one instance controls one output, the other heater output keeps heating through this e-stop, and the clone documents no independent stop (use the front panel or mains switch); the re-enable resumes heating toward the setpoint or manual output stored in the controller, unchecked by the envelope if set elsewhere. Upstream transport: one socket without a lock or resynchronisation, so concurrent reads can swap replies (SETP?, HTR? and MOUT? share one pattern; RANGE? takes any first digit) and after one late reply later commands can read the previous reply (the stop's OUTMODE? check is specific and fails safe); failures print to stdout, so do not serve the endpoint over stdio; no reconnect (after a dropped connection every command, the e-stop included, fails until a restart); no identity check of the instrument on host:port; native.py needs the clone mounted as the package devices and pythonSoftIOC, which the card's install block lacks. The clone has no licence or copyright statement in any file. The card's routing named the DP832 as its example; the override proposal narrows the entry symbol to the LS336.
